audit.whatIsWrong: CROSS-LAYER DISAGREEMENT: all seven phases[N].side read 'Skill' while all seven content win[N] read 'Aurora'. The page renders two different answers to who wins each stage.
audit.why: The packet levelChart is all-Aurora, every phases[N].why describes Aurora executing her pattern, and every whys[N] describes Aurora ahead (whys[0]: 'keeping you slightly ahead at level 1'). The prose on both layers agrees on Aurora, so the full-layer 'Skill' rows are the outlier. Resolved by moving all seven sides to Aurora; win[N] already reads Aurora on the content layer, so there is no matching content edit to propose — the pair is already at the target value.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0].why and phases[5].why are the generic Aurora template and both call Neeko 'his'.
audit.why: Level 1 the real fact is range: Blooming Burst is 800 against Aurora's 900 Q, so Aurora out-pokes her. At first item the punishable window is Tangle-Barbs, 12s at rank 1 and 10s at rank 5.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten with Neeko's own numbers and correct pronouns.

audit.why: The decisive interactions are already stated and match Riot's text: Tangle-Barbs (E) is the root at 1000 range and passes through everything it hits (minions do not stop it), growing if it kills a unit or passes a champion; Pop Blossom (R) is a 600-range knockup then stun whose preparation is HIDDEN while she is disguised; Inherent Glamour breaks on casting a damaging spell, on immobilizing CC, or when the copy takes damage equal to its health bar. No corrections needed here.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d is the tradeGood string pasted verbatim under 'Punish whiffs with the full pattern'.
audit.why: The title promises the punish window; the body just repeats the trade line. Replaced with the whiff window itself.
audit.corrected: A whiffed Tangle-Barbs is 12s of nothing — Q, E her step-up, Q-recast, hop out before it returns.

edits.before: Q-poke and recast on his last-hits — the spirit-mark detonation chips harder than the lane expects.
edits.after: Q-poke and recast on her last-hits — Blooming Burst is an 800 seed and does not out-range your 900.

edits.before: Luden's spike: the full Q-E-Q rotation chunks half bars. Force trades on his cooldown gaps.
edits.after: Luden's spike: the full Q-E-Q rotation chunks half bars. Force trades in Tangle-Barbs' 10s gap.

edits.before: Q the last-hit, E her step-up, Q-recast the slowed target, hop out before Tangle-Barbs is back at 12s.
edits.after: A whiffed Tangle-Barbs is 12s of nothing — Q, E her step-up, Q-recast, hop out before the root returns.

notes: The seven phases[N].side rows were the only cross-layer disagreement here: full said 'Skill', content win[N] said 'Aurora', and every why on both layers describes Aurora ahead. I moved the full layer to Aurora rather than the content layer to Skill, because moving win[N] to Skill would have required rewriting all seven whys against what the packet levelChart and the prose both say. No win[N] edit accompanies the side edits because win[N] is already 'Aurora' — the pair converges rather than needing a second write. Win rate is 48.16% over 517 games, which is softer than an all-Aurora chart implies; I left the ratings (5/10 to 6/10) alone since they already read as an even lane rather than a stomp.
